one_liner: GIMP/GEGL's C pixel-format and matrix+TRC colour-space converter. GIMP claims up to 10x over LCMS2; no published benchmark backs it, and an lcms2 test found babl slower.
what_it_does: babl converts buffers between pixel formats: data types (u8, u16, half, float, double), component orders, alpha association and colour models (RGB, Y, CIE Lab, HSV, CMYK and others), each tied to a colour space. You request a 'fish' between two formats with babl_fish(src, dst), or babl_fast_fish(src, dst, "fast") for a looser one, and call babl_process(fish, src, dst, n_pixels). RGB spaces come from built-in definitions (sRGB, Rec2020, Adobe, Apple, ProPhoto, DisplayP3) or from matrix+TRC ICC v2/v4 profiles via babl_space_from_icc. The API is unrelated to lcms2's cmsCreateTransform/cmsDoTransform, so it is not a drop-in replacement.
how_it_is_fast: babl does not walk a general ICC pipeline. For RGB-to-RGB between spaces it multiplies the source RGB-to-XYZ and destination XYZ-to-RGB matrices once into a single float 3x3 (babl-rgb-converter.c), and linearises u8 input through 256-entry TRC tables. Conversions are 'fishes' built from chains of registered fast-path converters. At runtime babl times candidate chains (searching up to BABL_PATH_LENGTH steps, 3 by default) and keeps the fastest one whose error against its 64-bit floating-point reference stays under BABL_TOLERANCE (0.0000047 in code). The choices are cached on disk in ~/.cache/babl/babl-fishes. Hot converters are compiled several times, for x86-64-v2/v3/v4 (SSE4.1, AVX2/F16C/FMA, AVX-512) and for NEON, and dispatched at runtime. Once a fish with 8-bit-per-channel input has processed 32,768 pixels, babl replaces it with a full 256^3 (or 256^2) lookup table, enabled by default on little-endian hosts (BABL_LUT).
when_to_use: GEGL or GIMP plug-ins, or any C program that converts pixel buffers between u8/u16/half/float encodings, alpha modes and RGB spaces in one call.
Matrix+TRC RGB-to-RGB conversion (sRGB, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto, Rec2020, display profiles without CLUTs), where babl folds the profile pair into one 3x3 plus TRC tables.
Long-running processes that convert many 8-bit images with the same format pair, where the automatic 256^3 lookup table pays off after its 32,768-pixel threshold.
Interactive previews where you can trade accuracy for speed with babl_fast_fish("fast"/"glitch") or a BABL_TOLERANCE of 0.01-0.1 (docs).
when_not_to_use: CMYK or other CLUT-based ICC work: babl hands every CMYK profile to lcms2 itself (cmsCreateTransform with TYPE_CMYKA_DBL to and from a linear scRGB profile, double precision, BPC on), so it adds a step on top of lcms2 rather than beating it.

RGB profiles whose A2B0/B2A0 CLUTs matter: babl_space_from_icc refuses them for relative colorimetric ('use lcms, accuracy desired and cluts are present') unless BABL_ICC_INTENT_PERFORMANCE is set, refuses explicit perceptual on CLUT profiles, and does not implement absolute colorimetric or saturation intents.

Choosing it on speed alone against lcms2: the only timed head-to-head found, from the Little CMS project (2019), had lcms2 at 3.59 s against babl at 6.36 s, and lcms2 with the fast_float plugin at 1.7 s (snippet only).
Memory-constrained hosts with BABL_LUT enabled: a single 8-bit RGBA fish can allocate 64 MiB (u8 out) or 256 MiB (float out) for its table, freed only after 5 minutes unused by default.

integration.form: shared lib (meson build; extensions are loaded from BABL_PATH as shared objects at runtime)
integration.dependencies: none required for RGB/gray; lcms2 >= 2.8 (optional, meson with-lcms) for CMYK ICC profiles; threads; optional gobject-introspection and vapigen for bindings
integration.min_toolchain: meson >= 0.60; C compiler with C11 atomics (MSVC built with /std:c11 since 0.1.126); gcc/clang on Linux, BSD and macOS
integration.platforms: x86-64 (runtime-dispatched v2/v3/v4 builds of SIMD extensions), aarch64 and 32-bit ARM NEON, i686, other little- and big-endian targets (LUTs disabled on big-endian); win32, Linux, BSDs, macOS; initial WASM support since 0.1.128
integration.thread_safety: Partly documented. Space creation from ICC is mutex-guarded (babl_space_mutex; 0.1.86 'improved thread safety for babl_space_from_icc', 0.1.78 fixed mutex and atomicity bugs). babl.h says babl_gc() must be called from the main thread with no concurrent babl processing in other threads, which implies processing may otherwise run in parallel.

gotchas: The first use of a new format pair runs a timed path search, and the result is persisted to ~/.cache/babl/babl-fishes keyed on version, BABL_PATH_LENGTH and BABL_TOLERANCE, so first-run and cache-miss latency differ from steady state.
The 256^3 LUT allocation in babl-fish-path.c (babl_fish_lut_process_maybe) is written to straight after malloc with no NULL check. Set BABL_LUT=0 where a 64-256 MiB allocation can fail.
The docs give the default BABL_TOLERANCE as 0.000001, but the code uses 0.0000047. babl_fast_fish results are not singletons and leak unless the caller caches them (babl.h).

LUT handling has had regressions: 0.1.102 disabled LUT code paths by default ('brown paper bag release'), 0.1.104 re-enabled them, 0.1.106 fixed 1bpp-to-4bpp LUTs, and 0.1.114 fixed a broken TRC cache for formula-based ICC TRCs and removed 'some broken conversions'.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick babl when you need GEGL-compatible pixel-format conversion (data type, alpha mode and matrix+TRC RGB space in one call) inside a C codebase. For ICC transforms with CMYK or CLUT profiles, use Little CMS 2 with its fast_float plugin (C) or moxcms (Rust); jsColorEngine covers the same ICC ground for JavaScript hosts.
verified_claims_summary: The only claim is first-party and comes without methodology: the GIMP 2.10 release notes (gimp.org, blocked here; WebSearch snippet) say babl is 'up to 10 times faster than LCMS2 for the cases tested', and a search-result summary adds that GIMP uses babl for ICC matrix-based conversions because it is 'an order of magnitude faster' than lcms2. No cases, timings, hardware or code are published. The babl tree holds no lcms2 comparison (tools/babl-benchmark.c times babl fishes alone in MPx/s on 1 Mi-pixel buffers), and the one reachable rebuttal (Little CMS blog, 2019-10-02, snippet only) measured babl at 6.36 s against lcms2 at 3.59 s, roughly 1.8x slower (derived from snippet). Any advantage is plausible only on matrix+TRC RGB paths: CMYK in babl runs through lcms2 itself.
status_note: Actively maintained in GNOME GitLab (0.1.128 released 2026-08-07; commits since then through 2026-10-03 are build and CI changes, mirrored read-only to GitHub with 25 stars). It is LGPL-3.0-or-later and a core GIMP/GEGL dependency, so it is safe to link dynamically, but the speed claim against lcms2 is unsubstantiated.
